speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; can you describe when you first noticed it and if it is painful, itchy, or burning?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Given your history of sun exposure, I need to know: has the lesion changed in size, color, or shape over time, and does it bleed or crust over?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand in a patient with significant sun exposure is highly suggestive of an actinic keratosis. To confirm this and rule out other possibilities, have you noticed any other similar spots on your face or arms, and do you recall any specific injury to that area?

I would like to perform a physical examination of the lesion to assess its borders, color variation, and surface texture more closely. Please hold your hand still while I examine the dorsal surface.

speaker: Doctor
text: The dermoscopy results are normal, which is somewhat atypical for a classic actinic keratosis but can occur in early or subtle cases. To further refine the diagnosis, have you experienced any numbness or tingling in that hand, and does the lesion feel hard or fixed to the underlying tissue?
